notes: The correlative גַּם … גַּם is rendered *whether … or*; because Hebrew writes a connective for each member, each takes only its own English word rather than one morpheme taking the pair (rule 14, on the אוֹ … אוֹ model).
*it* of *whether it be* is left `added` as an impersonal, not presentative, dummy (rule 20); the competing reading would fold *it be* whole into `אַהֲבָה`.
`לִפְנֵי` → *is before* fuses under rule 30, the construction-supplied copula joining the whole expression, headed on the construct noun.
Both object markers are `unrepresented` (rule 16) and both articles on `אָדָם` and `כֹּל` are `unrepresented`, the ASV writing bare *man* and *all* (rule 29).
